description: CSV parser and writer for JavaScript and TypeScript. csvloom/papa returns what Papa Parse 5.7.1 returns for a string; the main entry (parse, unparse, parseDetailed) is stricter about options; csvloom/stream has parseStream, a streaming parser built on async iterators. Zero dependencies, no eval.
rules: Pick the entry by the job: 'csvloom' has parse, unparse and parseDetailed as named exports only; 'csvloom/papa' (import Papa from 'csvloom/papa') is for existing Papa Parse code; 'csvloom/stream' has parseStream.

parse and Papa.parse take a string and return { data, errors, meta } synchronously. For a File, Blob, URL or stream use parseStream; step, chunk, complete, error, worker, download and encoding throw UnsupportedFeatureError.

parseStream returns an async iterator of batches { data, errors, meta }: read it with for await. A source is a string, file.stream(), response.body, a Node Readable, or an iterable of string or Uint8Array chunks; a bare Uint8Array is not a source, pass [bytes]. Bytes must be UTF-8.
Malformed CSV does not throw: read errors. In 'csvloom', an unknown option or a value of the wrong type throws a TypeError that names it.
A final line break gives one more record; pass skipEmptyLines: true unless you want it.
unparse from 'csvloom' escapes formula-like values by default (escapeFormulae: false turns it off); Papa.unparse from 'csvloom/papa' does not escape unless asked.
detect, positions, repair, schema and sepLine are options of parseDetailed and parseStream only; parse rejects them as unknown options.
For input you do not trust, use parseStream with maxRecordLength (it has no default), delimiter and newline.
Quote a speed number only with its lane and conditions from docs/benchmarks.md, and never as 'fastest'.
